data.name: Bullseye
data.detailed_description:
Que melhor maneira de matar o tempo do que disparar setas em um alvo no meio do oceano?

Bullseye tem dois modos de jogo: Relaxed e Parkour.

Descontraído:
Dê uma pausa e relaxe disparando flechas no meio do oceano calmo.

Parkour:
Salte as paredes e dispare no meio do ar para competir no Steam Leaderboards para o bullseye mais rápido!

10 níveis para cada modo. O tempo de reprodução médio é de 1 a 2 horas, variando de acordo com a qualidade do seu objetivo e com as conquistas e as altas pontuações desejadas.

reviews.review:
Bullseye is a very simple free game about shooting arrows at targets, but I actually like how focused it is. There is no huge story or complicated progression to get through. I am basically trying to hit targets as accurately as possible, with the game split between a relaxed mode and a parkour mode. The relaxed side gives me a calm environment in the middle of the ocean, while the parkour levels add movement and make me shoot while jumping around. It is a small idea, but it works well for short sessions.

The relaxed mode is probably what I enjoy most when I just want something easy to play. I can take my time lining up shots and concentrate on getting the bullseye instead of worrying about enemies or a timer. There are ten levels in this mode, and the peaceful ocean setting makes the whole thing feel quite different from a normal action game. I like that the game does not try to force excitement into every second. Sometimes having a simple target and trying to hit it accurately is enough.

The parkour mode gives the game a much better challenge. There are twenty levels where I have to jump off walls and shoot in mid air, with the fastest successful runs being tracked through Steam leaderboards. This changes the experience quite a bit because I am no longer just standing still and aiming. I have to think about movement and timing at the same time, which makes getting a clean shot feel much more satisfying. I also like that the two modes give me a choice between playing calmly and actually testing my aim.

The biggest problem is the amount of content. There are thirty levels in total, and the game itself says the average playthrough is around one to two hours depending on how much I care about achievements and high scores. That is not a bad amount for a free game, but it does mean I can see pretty much everything fairly quickly. Once I have finished the levels, there is not a huge amount of progression waiting for me. The Steam achievements and leaderboard times give me some reasons to replay them, but the game is still very much built around mastering what is already there rather than constantly giving me something new.

I also think the simplicity works against it in some ways. The shooting itself feels fine, but there are not many mechanics beyond aiming, firing and moving through the parkour sections. I cannot build a character, unlock a large collection of equipment or explore a bigger world. Normally that would be a major weakness for me, but I do not think Bullseye is trying to be that kind of game. I would rather it stay focused than add a load of pointless systems just to make the game appear bigger.

The presentation is basic but I think it suits the idea. The calm ocean gives the relaxed levels a nice atmosphere, while the parkour sections are more about movement and timing. There are also only five Steam achievements, so even the achievement side is kept fairly small. This is definitely a game I would play when I want something quick rather than something I am going to spend dozens of hours with. The fact that it is free makes the short length much easier for me to accept.

Overall, Bullseye is a simple game that knows exactly what it wants to be. I like the relaxing target shooting, the more demanding parkour mode and the fact that the controls and objective are so easy to understand. The main thing holding it back is the limited content, because once I have worked through the thirty levels there is not much left apart from improving my scores. Still, I think the free price, clean concept and difference between the two modes make it worth trying when I want a short and casual game. It is not deep enough for one of my higher ratings, but I think it does its small idea well.

Rating: 7.3/10
